corrections.caveats: (1) Snippet only: the paper (arXiv 1412.7580, 'Fast Convolutional Nets With fbfft: A GPU Performance Evaluation') could not be opened here (arXiv, iclr.cc, ACM, IEEE egress-blocked), so the GPU model, cuFFT version, and whether the 1.51x mean is for FFT kernels alone are unverified; the ICLR 2015 venue is stated by the search record but not by any opened page (the fbcunn README links only arXiv). Retier to B if a session with arXiv access confirms the peer-reviewed venue and tables. (2) fbcuda holds only the kernels (fbfft/FBFFT.cuh, FBFFTCommon.cuh, FBFFTParameters.h and the 2D/inverse headers) with no cuFFT comparison or driver; the convolution modules and test/benchmark_fft.lua (a size sweep over SpatialConvolutionCuFFT with no published results) live in facebookarchive/fbcunn, archived 2022-01-13. (3) soumith/convnet-benchmarks (maintained by fbfft co-author Soumith Chintala, so not independent) shows fbfft convolutions beating CuDNN R2 in April 2015 (256 ms vs 1019 ms layer-wise total) but losing to CuDNN R4 fp32 on Titan X for AlexNet (104 ms vs 81 ms); that is convolution vs cuDNN, not FFT vs cuFFT. (4) 2014-2015 GPUs and cuFFT versions; modern cuFFT and cuDNN FFT/Winograd paths may have closed the gap. (5) cuFFT is not one of the assignment's baselines (FFTW, MKL FFT, KissFFT). (6) License is BSD-3-Clause plus Facebook's 'Additional Grant of Patent Rights Version 2' (PATENTS file, with a termination clause). (7) Repository archived 2020-03-03; last commit 2018-05-29 ('Upgrade - fbcode'), read from the github.com commits page.

tier_reason: The venue is confirmed as peer-reviewed (the README cites KDD 2021, pp. 1309-1318, and links the ACM DOI), but I could not open the paper (dl.acm.org, arXiv and the author site are egress-blocked) and could not confirm that the 'order of magnitude' snippet is the KDD abstract rather than the arXiv preprint, so per the snippet-only rule it drops to C. The repo has no timing harness (PFT.cpp prints coefficients and L2 error only; FFTW.cpp never reads its timers), so A is unavailable.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Per the authors' KDD 2021 paper (text seen only as a search snippet, not on any opened page): an order of magnitude speedup for sufficiently small output sizes without sacrificing accuracy, outperforming FFTW, MKL, pruned FFT and Goertzel. No number appears in the repo.
corrections.caveats: (1) Snippet only: the paper (ACM DOI 10.1145/3447548.3467293, arXiv 2008.12559) could not be opened here (dl.acm.org, arXiv, openreview and yongchanpark.github.io are egress-blocked; the yongchanpark.github.io GitHub repo holds only an empty README), so CPU model, compiler, flags and the actual ratios are unknown. The KDD 2021 venue itself is confirmed by the repo README's citation. Retier to B if a session with ACM or arXiv access confirms the abstract and tables. (2) No timing harness in the repo: src/PFT.cpp prints the first and last coefficients and the relative L2 error against the MKL DFTI full FFT and has no timers; src/FFTW.cpp declares clock_t variables but never reads them; src/PrunedFFTW.cpp is the FFTW pruned-FFT web-page pseudocode and does not compile as is; src/goertzel.c is copied from pramasoul/jrand. (3) The FFTW baseline in src/FFTW.cpp is a 1,048,576-point float r2c transform on 4 threads planned with FFTW_ESTIMATE (FFTW_MEASURE only in a comment), weaker than a tuned FFTW; it includes the Windows-only tchar.h. (4) PFT.cpp's header says the example is designed for real-valued input with a target range centered at zero; other ranges need the modification described in the paper. (5) Building needs Intel MKL and IPP (proprietary but freely redistributable) in addition to the Apache-2.0 code. (6) Last commit 2025-08-19 is a README edit; the last source change is 'Update PFT.cpp' on 2021-06-03 (github.com commits page). (7) Follow-up multidimensional work (snudatalab/Auto-MPFT, KDD 2024) was not opened.

notes: Downgraded B to C: KDD 2021 (peer-reviewed) is confirmed by the README, but the speedup text is snippet only and the paper could not be opened. Metadata (Apache-2.0, 16 stars, 3 forks, last commit 2025-08-19, stale) confirmed.

tier_reason: benchmarks/efft_benchmark.cpp does pair eFFT against an FFTW 2D baseline, but no results are published anywhere I could open (README, repo files, PyPI description); the TPAMI and JORS papers are egress-blocked and the only snippet seen gives absolute eFFT times, not a ratio against FFTW, so no comparative number is available: D.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No comparative numbers published in the repo or on any opened page. The README says FFTW3 'served as the benchmark for testing and evaluation' and benchmarks/efft_benchmark.cpp pairs BenchmarkFeedWithEvents/BenchmarkFeedWithPackets with FFTW versions; CI runs that target (ci.yaml 'Benchmark' step) but results are not committed. A TPAMI abstract snippet (not opened) gives absolute eFFT times only (< 1 microsecond per event for packets of more than 40 events at 128 x 128).
corrections.caveats: (1) No benchmark numbers or CPU model appear in the repo, README, PyPI description or any page I could open; the TPAMI paper (doi 10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3422209), the JORS paper (doi 10.5334/jors.642, openresearchsoftware.metajnl.com) and Zenodo are egress-blocked. The abstract snippet gives absolute eFFT times only (PSNR > 55 dB, SSIM > 0.999; < 1 microsecond per event for packets > 40 events and < 0.5 microsecond for > 200 events at 128 x 128), not a ratio against FFTW. Retier to B if the TPAMI paper's FFTW comparison is read. (2) The in-repo FFTW baseline is deliberately weak: initializeGroundTruth plans fftw_plan_dft_2d with FFTW_ESTIMATE | FFTW_UNALIGNED | FFTW_NO_SIMD | FFTW_PRESERVE_INPUT, runs in double precision while eFFT uses float, and recomputes the whole N x N transform for every event (or packet); getGroundTruthFFT() also casts and transposes the row-major double result into a float Eigen matrix. Both benchmark sides copy the result into a new matrix (auto result = efft.getFFT() copies too), so the copy cost is roughly symmetric apart from the cast. In CI FFTW comes from the distro package, so the -O3 -march=native -ffast-math flags apply only to eFFT. (3) Different problem from a plain FFT: incremental exact update after sparse input changes versus a from-scratch transform, meaningful only for event-stream use. (4) Events are seeded from std::random_device, so runs are not bit-reproducible. (5) Last commit 2026-09-22 ('Update .gitignore'), read from the github.com commits page; PyPI efft 1.0.5 lists GPL-3.0-later while the header and GitHub say GPL v3.

notes: Downgraded C to D: a paired FFTW benchmark exists but no comparative number is on any reachable page. Not rejected: a TPAMI 2024 paper and a PyPI package make it referenced, and the keep-and-document rule applies; metadata (GPL-3.0, 23 stars, 2 forks, active) confirmed.
